text: Claims of discrimination during employment have nothing to do with “dismissal.” [Melugin v. Zurich Canada, supra, 50 CA4th at 668-669, 57 CR2d at 787] 1) [3:475] Rationale: “The mere act of unintentionally discriminating against someone in violation of the law cannot be an ‘offense’ negating the very coverage granted to the insured for claims of ‘discrimination’ by the policy itself … [That] would result in an entirely fictional grant of coverage, by which the express grant of coverage for claims of discrimination would be empty and idle because such claims in all cases would be barred by section 533 or by inapplicable policy exclusions.” [Melugin v. Zurich Canada, supra, 50 CA4th at 669, 57 CR2d at 787-788 (emphasis added)] [3:476 - 3:484] Reserved. c. [3:485] No duty to defend EEOC or FEHA administrative proceedings: The standard-form CGL policy obligates the insurer to defend “suits” against the insured and defines “suit” as a “civil proceeding in which damages … to which this insurance applies are alleged” (including arbitration and other ADR proceedings if the insurer consents).
